title: The Fox and the Grapes
summary: A hungry fox wants some grapes, but they are too high for him.

source.author: Aesop
source.note: Retold from the plot of the fable in new A1 English by Lexkite; no sentences copied from any translation.

license: Adaptation CC BY 4.0 Lexkite; original fable in the public domain

cover.scene: Flat 2D illustration: an orange fox sitting under a tall green vine with purple grapes, warm summer sky, no text

chapters.title: Too High
sentences: It is a hot summer day.
A fox walks in a big garden.
He is very hungry and thirsty.
He sees some grapes on a tall plant.
The grapes are purple and sweet.
The fox jumps, but he cannot get them.
The grapes are too high for him.
Now the fox is hot, sad and angry.
He looks up at the grapes.
"They are sour, and I do not want them."
Then he walks away with an empty stomach.

quiz.explain: The fox is hungry and wants to eat the grapes on the tall plant.

quiz.q: Can the fox get the grapes?
quiz.explain: The story says the grapes are too high for him.

quiz.q: Why does the fox say the grapes are sour?
options: He cannot get them, so he says they are bad.
quiz.explain: He never tastes them. He says they are sour because he cannot reach them – this is the lesson of the fable.
